assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a structurally simple, solution-processable crystalline family into photovoltaic absorbers with efficiencies rivaling silicon within a decade. Structure-property design (composition, dimensionality, defect tolerance) is central, and the field has reshaped materials chemistry and energy research.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers (2009), Park and Grätzel made the solid-state cell (2012), and Snaith's group showed the mesosuperstructured and planar architectures. The supplied list does not include Kojima, so a configuration from the credited names is contestable, and Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok also have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency records are independently reproduced worldwide and commercial tandem development is advancing, so impact is clear. Long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain open, which argues for some caution on timing.
uncertainties: Stability and toxicity may not be resolved enough for a mature verdict
Credit split among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is disputed
Kojima is absent from the credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is one of the most widely used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceuticals and materials, enabled by systematic ligand design. It is a clear case of a method that a whole community adopted.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the general, ligand-controlled amination; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but less general. Two laureates is a clean and defensible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of use, with robust independent confirmation and industrial scale-up. The Pd cross-coupling area was recognized in 2010, so a novelty argument against it exists but the C-N chemistry is distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 prize may be argued by some members
Precursor contribution of Kosugi and Migita is not fully weighed here

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-field DNP raised NMR sensitivity by orders of magnitude, enabling structural studies of materials surfaces, amyloids and membrane proteins that were otherwise inaccessible. It is a strong enabling method with a physical-chemistry core.
assessment.attribution: Griffin built the gyrotron-based high-field DNP and introduced biradical polarizing agents; Emsley drove its application to materials and surfaces. Bodenhausen and Prisner contributed dissolution DNP and high-field EPR/DNP instrumentation, so credit is spread over several groups.
assessment.maturity: Commercial instruments are in routine use and the technique is well confirmed. Impact is still growing, especially in materials, which supports timing.
uncertainties: Allocation among Griffin, Emsley, Bodenhausen and Prisner is uncertain
Early solid-state DNP precursors (Abragam, Wind, Griffin) may complicate priority

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert single bases without double-strand breaks, a new chemical-biology tool with immediate therapeutic use. The importance is high and the underlying molecular design is chemical.
assessment.attribution: Liu directed the work; Komor made the cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor, which required directed evolution of a TadA deaminase. Liu is the obvious central figure, and a trio is tenable but trainee inclusion is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials and broad use confirm utility, but clinical outcomes are early. Prime editing (a separate candidate) and CRISPR itself (2020) raise questions about overlap with prior recognition.
uncertainties: Relation to the 2020 CRISPR prize may count against it
Whether trainees should share credit is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic structures of nitrogenase and the discovery of the interstitial carbide in the FeMo cofactor underpin understanding of biological N2 reduction. The structural evidence is rigorous and the problem is a fundamental one.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the structural work from the 1992 MoFe-protein structure; Einsle contributed the high-resolution cofactor and the carbide. Dean, Ribbe and Seefeldt contributed mechanism and biochemistry, so a structural-only prize would omit them.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed independently, but the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site remain debated, so the story is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Structure versus mechanism credit is unresolved

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native MS lets intact non-covalent protein complexes be weighed and their stoichiometry and topology read out, now a routine structural-biology complement to cryo-EM and X-ray. It enabled whole communities to analyze assemblies and membrane proteins.
assessment.attribution: Robinson extended it to large machines and membrane proteins in lipids, and Heck to heterogeneous assemblies and Orbitrap-based native MS. Chait, Loo and Gross have strong early claims, and Fenn and Tanaka's 2002 prize covers ionization.
assessment.maturity: Mature with broad adoption and commercial instruments, though its structural content is lower-resolution than the structural methods.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for biomolecule ionization
Credit among five names is crowded

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography allows structures from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved dynamics before radiation damage. Like 3D electron diffraction, it makes structure determination possible where conventional crystals are not available.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first demonstration, Fromme the photosystem I work, and Hajdu the diffraction-before-destruction concept. Schlichting's time-resolved studies are also important, and the credit is plausible for three.
assessment.maturity: XFEL access is limited and results are strong but confined to few facilities. Time-resolved studies are still emerging, so the maturity is intermediate.
uncertainties: Credit is shared among several leaders including Schlichting
Chemical, rather than physics or biology, framing may be questioned

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glues exploit the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade proteins on demand, expanding the druggable space. Clinical molecules are in late-stage trials, and the concept is chemically original.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced PROTACs (2001), Ciulli contributed structure-guided VHL ligands and mechanistic insight. The molecular-glue side (Handa, Ito, Gray) is separate and would complicate a single prize.
assessment.maturity: Approved drugs do not yet exist, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Joint credit with molecular glue/thalidomide mechanism is unresolved
